pnle-set1-part2.explanation: The expected due date establishes gestational age, which immediately guides assessment of labor, fetal maturity, and potential obstetric priorities.

pnle-set1-part2.question: A neonate begins to gag and turns a dusky color. What should the nurse do first?
choices: Provide oxygen via face mask as ordered
Aspirate the neonate’s nose and mouth with a bulb syringe.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Gagging with dusky coloration suggests airway obstruction from secretions. The immediate nursing action is to clear the airway with a bulb syringe, beginning with the mouth and then the nose.

pnle-set1-part2.question: When a client states that her “water broke,” which of the following actions would be inappropriate for the nurse to do?
choices: Observing the pooling of straw-colored fluid.
Checking vaginal discharge with nitrazine paper.
Conducting a bedside ultrasound for an amniotic fluid index.
Observing for flakes of vernix in the vaginal discharge.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: A bedside ultrasound for amniotic fluid volume is not the routine first-line confirmation of rupture of membranes. Pooling, nitrazine testing, and ferning/vernix observations can support assessment.

pnle-set1-part2.question: A baby girl is born 8 weeks premature. At birth, she has no spontaneous respirations but is successfully resuscitated. Within several hours she develops respiratory grunting, cyanosis, tachypnea, nasal flaring, and retractions. She’s diagnosed with respiratory distress syndrome, intubated, and placed on a ventilator. Which nursing action should be included in the baby’s plan of care to prevent retinopathy of prematurity?
choices: Cover his eyes while receiving oxygen.
Monitor partial pressure of oxygen (Pao2) levels.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Retinopathy of prematurity is associated with excessive or fluctuating oxygen exposure. Monitoring PaO2 and carefully controlling oxygen delivery helps avoid hyperoxia.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Which of the following is normal newborn calorie intake?
choices: 30 to 40 calories per lb of body weight.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Newborns generally require about 110–130 kcal/kg/day for growth. Caloric needs are higher per kilogram than those of older children and adults.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Nurse John is knowledgeable that usually individual twins will grow appropriately and at the same rate as singletons until how many weeks?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Twin fetal growth generally parallels singleton growth during the earlier part of gestation, with growth restriction becoming more common after about 30–32 weeks.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Which of the following classifications applies to monozygotic twins for whom the cleavage of the fertilized ovum occurs more than 13 days after fertilization?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Very late division of a monozygotic embryo, more than about 13 days after fertilization, can be incomplete and produce conjoined twins.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Tyra experienced painless vaginal bleeding has just been diagnosed as having a placenta previa. Which of the following procedures is usually performed to diagnose placenta previa?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Ultrasound is the standard diagnostic method for locating the placenta and identifying placenta previa. Digital vaginal examination is avoided until previa is excluded because it can provoke severe hemorrhage.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Nurse Arnold knows that the following changes in respiratory functioning during pregnancy is considered normal:
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Pregnancy increases tidal volume and minute ventilation. Oxygen consumption also increases, while inspiratory capacity is not decreased as a normal primary change.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Emily has gestational diabetes and it is usually managed by which of the following therapy?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Management of gestational diabetes begins with medical nutrition therapy, physical activity as appropriate, and glucose monitoring. Insulin is added when glycemic targets are not achieved with lifestyle measures.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Magnesium sulfate is given to Jemma with preeclampsia to prevent which of the following condition?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Magnesium sulfate is used for seizure prophylaxis in severe preeclampsia and for treatment/prevention of eclamptic seizures.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Cammile with sickle cell anemia has an increased risk for having a sickle cell crisis during pregnancy. Aggressive management of a sickle cell crisis includes which of the following measures?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Hydration with appropriate IV fluids helps reduce blood viscosity and supports perfusion during vaso-occlusive crisis. Pain control and oxygen when hypoxemic are also important.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Which of the following drugs is the antidote for magnesium toxicity?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: IV calcium gluconate antagonizes the neuromuscular and cardiac effects of excessive magnesium and is the standard antidote for magnesium toxicity.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Marlyn is screened for tuberculosis during her first prenatal visit. An intradermal injection of purified protein derivative (PPD) of the tuberculin bacilli is given. She is considered to have a positive test for which of the following results?
choices: An indurated wheal under 10 mm in diameter appears in 6 to 12 hours.
An indurated wheal over 10 mm in diameter appears in 48 to 72 hours.
A flat circumcised area under 10 mm in diameter appears in 6 to 12 hours.
A flat circumcised area over 10 mm in diameter appears in 48 to 72 hours.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: A tuberculin skin test is read 48–72 hours after placement and measures induration, not redness. In a person without special risk factors, 10 mm or more is considered positive; therefore an induration over 10 mm at 48–72 hours fits the choice.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Dianne, 24 year-old is 27 weeks’ pregnant arrives at her physician’s office with complaints of fever, nausea, vomiting, malaise, unilateral flank pain, and costovertebral angle tenderness. Which of the following diagnoses is most likely?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Fever, systemic symptoms, flank pain, and costovertebral angle tenderness strongly indicate acute pyelonephritis rather than asymptomatic bacteriuria or uncomplicated lower UTI.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Rh isoimmunization in a pregnant client develops during which of the following conditions?
choices: Rh-positive maternal blood crosses into fetal blood, stimulating fetal antibodies.
Rh-positive fetal blood crosses into maternal blood, stimulating maternal antibodies.
Rh-negative fetal blood crosses into maternal blood, stimulating maternal antibodies.
Rh-negative maternal blood crosses into fetal blood, stimulating fetal antibodies.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Rh isoimmunization occurs when Rh-positive fetal red cells enter an Rh-negative maternal circulation and stimulate maternal anti-D antibody production.

pnle-set1-part2.question: To promote comfort during labor, the nurse John advises a client to assume certain positions and avoid others. Which position may cause maternal hypotension and fetal hypoxia?
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: The supine position can compress the inferior vena cava, reducing venous return, maternal cardiac output, and uteroplacental perfusion. This can cause maternal hypotension and fetal hypoxia.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Celeste who used heroin during her pregnancy delivers a neonate. When assessing the neonate, the nurse Lhynnette expects to find:
choices: A flattened nose, small eyes, and thin lips.
Congenital defects such as limb anomalies.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Neonates exposed to opioids in utero commonly develop neonatal opioid withdrawal, characterized by irritability, tremors, poor feeding, high-pitched crying, and sleep disturbance.

pnle-set1-part2.question: The uterus returns to the pelvic cavity in which of the following time frames?
choices: When the lochia changes to alba.
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: The uterus descends into the true pelvis by approximately 10–14 days, and traditional nursing references often describe it as returning to the pelvic cavity by about the 7th–9th postpartum day.

pnle-set1-part2.question: Maureen, a primigravida client, age 20, has just completed a difficult, forceps-assisted delivery of twins. Her labor was unusually long and required oxytocin (Pitocin) augmentation. The nurse who’s caring for her should stay alert for:
pnle-set1-part2.explanation: Prolonged labor, uterine overdistention from twins, and oxytocin augmentation can fatigue the uterine muscle and increase the risk of uterine atony, the leading cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Michelle should know that the drainage is normal 4 days after a sigmoid colostomy when the stool is:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Normal bowel function and soft-formed stool usually do not occur until around the seventh day following surgery. Stool consistency is related to how much water is being absorbed.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Where would nurse Kristine place the call light for a male client with a right-sided brain attack and left homonymous hemianopsia?
choices: Directly in front of the client
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The client has left visual field blindness, so the call light should be placed on the client’s right side where it can be seen.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client is admitted to the emergency department following an accident. What are the first nursing actions of the nurse?
choices: Align the spine, check pupils, and check for hemorrhage.
Check respirations, stabilize spine, and check circulation.
Assess level of consciousness and circulation.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Checking respirations is an airway and breathing priority, while a possible neck injury requires spinal stabilization before further assessment.

pnle-set1-part3.question: In evaluating the effect of nitroglycerin, Nurse Arthur should know that it reduces preload and relieves angina by:
choices: Increasing contractility and slowing heart rate.
Increasing AV conduction and heart rate.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Nitroglycerin causes vasodilation, which decreases venous return (preload) and reduces the workload of the heart.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Patricia finds a female client who is post-myocardial infarction (MI) slumped on the side rails of the bed and unresponsive to shaking or shouting. Which is the nurse next action?
choices: Call for help and note the time.
Give two sharp thumps to the precordium, and check the pulse.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: After establishing that the client is unresponsive, the nurse should immediately call for help and note the time as a baseline for the cardiac-arrest response.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Monett is caring for a client recovering from gastro-intestinal bleeding. The nurse should:
choices: Plan care so the client can receive 8 hours of uninterrupted sleep each night.
Make sure that the client takes food and medications at prescribed intervals.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Food and prescribed drug therapy help prevent accumulation of gastric hydrochloric acid or neutralize and buffer acid that does accumulate.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client was on warfarin (Coumadin) before admission, and has been receiving heparin I.V. for 2 days. The partial thromboplastin time (PTT) is 68 seconds. What should Nurse Carla do?
choices: Stop the I.V. infusion of heparin and notify the physician.
Expect the warfarin to increase the PTT.
Increase the dosage, because the level is lower than normal.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source states that heparin is monitored by PTT and that the therapeutic level is about 1.5 to 2 times normal. A PTT of 68 seconds is therefore treated as therapeutic in this question.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A client undergone ileostomy, when should the drainage appliance be applied to the stoma?
choices: 24 hours later, when edema has subsided.
After the ileostomy begin to function.
When the client is able to begin self-care procedures.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The drainage appliance is applied in the operating room because ileostomy drainage contains digestive enzymes that can rapidly irritate and excoriate surrounding skin.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A client undergone spinal anesthetic, it will be important that the nurse immediately position the client in:
choices: On the side, to prevent obstruction of airway by tongue.
On the back, with knees flexed 15 degrees.
Flat on the stomach, with the head turned to the side.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The client is kept flat in a supine position for the specified postoperative period to reduce the risk of spinal headache associated with cerebrospinal-fluid leakage.

pnle-set1-part3.question: While monitoring a male client several hours after a motor vehicle accident, which assessment data suggest increasing intracranial pressure?
choices: Blood pressure is decreased from 160/90 to 110/70.
Pulse is increased from 87 to 95, with an occasional skipped beat.
The client is oriented when aroused from sleep, and goes back to sleep immediately.
The client refuses dinner because of anorexia.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A decreasing level of consciousness is an important sign of increasing intracranial pressure. Being immediately sleepy again after arousal suggests deteriorating neurologic status.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mrs. Cruz, 80 years old is diagnosed with pneumonia. Which of the following symptoms may appear first?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Older adults with pneumonia may initially present with altered mental status and dehydration because of a blunted immune response rather than classic respiratory symptoms.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client has active tuberculosis (TB). Which of the following symptoms will be exhibit?
choices: Chills, fever, night sweats, and hemoptysis
Fever of more than 104°F (40°C) and nausea
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Typical active TB symptoms include chills, fever, night sweats, and hemoptysis. The other combinations are not characteristic of active TB.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mark, a 7-year-old client is brought to the emergency department. He’s tachypneic and afebrile and has a respiratory rate of 36 breaths/minute and has a nonproductive cough. He recently had a cold. Form this history; the client may have which of the following conditions?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The history and symptoms are most consistent with acute asthma. The client is young and afebrile, making COPD, emphysema, and bronchial pneumonia less likely in this context.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Marichu was given morphine sulfate for pain. She is sleeping and her respiratory rate is 4 breaths/minute. If action isn’t taken quickly, she might have which of the following reactions?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Morphine can cause severe respiratory depression. A respiratory rate of 4 breaths/minute indicates a potentially life-threatening progression to respiratory arrest.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 77-year-old male client is admitted for elective knee surgery. Physical examination reveals shallow respirations but no sign of respiratory distress. Which of the following is a normal physiologic change related to aging?
choices: Increased elastic recoil of the lungs
Increased number of functional capillaries in the alveoli
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Normal aging is associated with decreased lung elastic recoil, fewer functional alveolar capillaries, increased residual volume, and decreased vital capacity.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse John is caring for a male client receiving lidocaine I.V. Which factor is the most relevant to administration of this medication?
choices: Decrease in arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) when measured with a pulse oximeter.
Presence of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) on a cardiac monitor.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: IV lidocaine is commonly used as an antiarrhythmic for ventricular dysrhythmias such as PVCs, making the cardiac-monitor finding most relevant.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Ron is caring for a male client taking an anticoagulant. The nurse should teach the client to:
choices: Avoid foods high in vitamin K
Use a straight razor when shaving.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source teaches avoiding large amounts of vitamin K because it can interfere with anticoagulation. A straight razor and aspirin can increase bleeding risk.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Lhynnette is preparing a site for the insertion of an I.V. catheter. The nurse should treat excess hair at the site by:
choices: Clipping the hair in the area
Removing the hair with a depilatory.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Excess hair should be clipped rather than shaved because shaving can cause skin abrasions and depilatories can irritate the skin.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Michelle is caring for an elderly female with osteoporosis. When teaching the client, the nurse should include information about which major complication:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Bone fracture is a major complication of osteoporosis because loss of bone mineral increases skeletal fragility. Dowager’s hump results from vertebral fractures.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Len is teaching a group of women to perform BSE. The nurse should explain that the purpose of performing the examination is to discover:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Breast self-examination is intended to help women recognize changes from previous examinations. A clinician is needed to diagnose whether a lump is malignant or benign.

pnle-set1-part3.question: When caring for a female client who is being treated for hyperthyroidism, it is important to:
choices: Provide extra blankets and clothing to keep the client warm.
Monitor the client for signs of restlessness, sweating, and excessive weight loss during thyroid replacement therapy.
Balance the client’s periods of activity and rest.
Encourage the client to be active to prevent constipation.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Clients with hyperthyroidism can be hyperactive and intolerant of heat, so balancing periods of activity and rest helps prevent excessive fatigue.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Kris is teaching a client with history of atherosclerosis. To decrease the risk of atherosclerosis, the nurse should encourage the client to:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Increasing activity supports cardiovascular health and helps manage risk factors such as excess weight. A low-cholesterol diet and stress reduction are also important.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Greta is working on a surgical floor. Nurse Greta must logroll a client following a:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A client after spinal surgery such as a laminectomy should be logrolled to keep the spinal column aligned during turning.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 55-year old client underwent cataract removal with intraocular lens implant. Nurse Oliver is giving the client discharge instructions. These instructions should include which of the following?
choices: Avoid lifting objects weighing more than 5 lb (2.25 kg).
Lie on your abdomen when in bed
Avoiding straining during bowel movement or bending at the waist.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Straining, heavy lifting, and bending at the waist can increase intraocular pressure. The client should avoid these activities during recovery.

pnle-set1-part3.question: George should be taught about testicular examinations during:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Testicular cancer commonly occurs in younger men, especially around ages 20 to 30. Teaching testicular self-examination before age 20 is the source's recommended timing.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client undergone a colon resection. While turning him, wound dehiscence with evisceration occurs. Nurse Trish first response is to:
choices: Place a saline-soaked sterile dressing on the wound.
Take a blood pressure and pulse.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The nurse should immediately cover the exposed tissue with a sterile saline-moistened dressing to prevent drying and contamination, then notify the physician and assess vital signs.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Audrey is caring for a client who has suffered a severe cerebrovascular accident. During routine assessment, the nurse notices Cheyne-Strokes respirations. Cheyne-strokes respirations are:
choices: A progressively deeper breaths followed by shallower breaths with apneic periods.
Rapid, deep breathing with abrupt pauses between each breath.
Rapid, deep breathing and irregular breathing without pauses.
Shallow breathing with an increased respiratory rate.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Cheyne-Stokes respirations progressively deepen and then become shallower, followed by periods of apnea. This differs from Biot’s and Kussmaul’s patterns.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Bea is assessing a male client with heart failure. The breath sounds commonly auscultated in clients with heart failure are:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Fine crackles commonly occur when fluid accumulates in the alveoli, as can happen with heart failure.

pnle-set1-part3.question: The nurse is caring for Kenneth experiencing an acute asthma attack. The client stops wheezing and breath sounds aren’t audible. The reason for this change is that:
choices: The airways are so swollen that no air cannot get through.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: In a severe asthma attack, wheezing may disappear because airway swelling and obstruction become so severe that little or no air can move through the airways. This is an emergency finding.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mike with epilepsy is having a seizure. During the active seizure phase, the nurse should:
choices: Place the client on his back remove dangerous objects, and insert a bite block.
Place the client on his side, remove dangerous objects, and insert a bite block.
Place the client o his back, remove dangerous objects, and hold down his arms.
Place the client on his side, remove dangerous objects, and protect his head.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: During an active seizure, place the client on the side, remove nearby hazards, and protect the head. Do not insert a bite block or restrain the client.

pnle-set1-part3.question: After insertion of a cheat tube for a pneumothorax, a client becomes hypotensive with neck vein distention, tracheal shift, absent breath sounds, and diaphoresis. Nurse Amanda suspects a tension pneumothorax has occurred. What cause of tension pneumothorax should the nurse check for?
choices: Excessive water in the water-seal chamber
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A kinked or obstructed chest tube can prevent air from escaping, allowing pressure to build and producing a tension pneumothorax.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Maureen is talking to a male client, the client begins choking on his lunch. He’s coughing forcefully. The nurse should:
choices: Stand him up and perform the abdominal thrust maneuver from behind.
Lay him down, straddle him, and perform the abdominal thrust maneuver.
Stay with him but not intervene at this time.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: If the client is coughing forcefully, the airway is not completely obstructed. The nurse should stay with the client and monitor rather than immediately perform abdominal thrusts. If complete obstruction occurs, appropriate choking intervention is required.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Ron is taking a health history of an 84 year old client. Which information will be most useful to the nurse for planning care?
choices: General health for the last 10 years.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Current health-promotion activities are especially useful for planning care because they identify the older client’s present positive health measures and needs.

pnle-set1-part3.question: When performing oral care on a comatose client, Nurse Krina should:
choices: Apply lemon glycerin to the client’s lips at least every 2 hours.
Brush the teeth with client lying supine.
Place the client in a side lying position, with the head of the bed lowered.
Clean the client’s mouth with hydrogen peroxide.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A side-lying position with the head of the bed lowered helps prevent aspiration of oral secretions during oral care. Hydrogen peroxide and prolonged lemon-glycerin use can damage or dry oral tissues.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 77-year-old male client is admitted with a diagnosis of dehydration and change in mental status. He’s being hydrated with L.V. fluids. When the nurse takes his vital signs, she notes he has a fever of 103°F (39.4°C) a cough producing yellow sputum and pleuritic chest pain. The nurse suspects this client may have which of the following conditions?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Fever, productive cough, and pleuritic chest pain are common findings of pneumonia. A sputum culture may be obtained to help confirm the suspected infection.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Oliver is working in an out patient clinic. He has been alerted that there is an outbreak of tuberculosis (TB). Which of the following clients entering the clinic today most likely to have TB?
choices: A 43-yesr-old homeless man with a history of alcoholism
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: People who are economically disadvantaged, malnourished, or have reduced immunity have increased risk for TB. A homeless client with alcoholism fits these risk factors.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Virgie with a positive Mantoux test result will be sent for a chest X-ray. The nurse is aware that which of the following reasons this is done?
choices: To determine if a repeat skin test is needed
To determine the extent of lesions
To determine if this is a primary or secondary infection
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A chest X-ray can show the presence and extent of pulmonary lesions. The source states that sputum culture confirms the diagnosis and a chest X-ray cannot determine primary versus secondary infection.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Kennedy with acute asthma showing inspiratory and expiratory wheezes and a decreased forced expiratory volume should be treated with which of the following classes of medication right away?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Bronchodilators are the first-line class for immediate relief of acute bronchoconstriction. Beta blockers can worsen bronchoconstriction, while steroids address inflammation but are not immediate rescue therapy.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mr. Vasquez 56-year-old client with a 40-year history of smoking one to two packs of cigarettes per day has a chronic cough producing thick sputum, peripheral edema and cyanotic nail beds. Based on this information, he most likely has which of the following conditions?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The long smoking history, chronic productive cough, cyanosis, and peripheral edema are most consistent with chronic obstructive bronchitis.

pnle-set1-part3.question: The treatment for patients with leukemia is bone marrow transplantation. Which statement about bone marrow transplantation is not correct?
choices: The patient is under local anesthesia during the procedure
The aspirated bone marrow is mixed with heparin.
The aspiration site is the posterior or anterior iliac crest.
The recipient receives cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan) for 4 consecutive days before the procedure.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source states that the patient receives general anesthesia during the transplant procedure, making the statement about local anesthesia incorrect.

pnle-set1-part3.question: After several days of admission, Francis becomes disoriented and complains of frequent headaches. The nurse in-charge first action would be:
choices: Document the patient’s status in his charts.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A disoriented patient is at increased risk for falling. The source identifies raising the side rails as the initial safety action.

pnle-set1-part3.question: During routine care, Francis asks the nurse, “How can I be anemic if this disease causes increased my white blood cell production?” The nurse in-charge best response would be that the increased number of white blood cells (WBC) is:
choices: Are not responsible for the anemia.
Have an abnormally short life span of cells.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source explains that excessive white blood cell production crowds out red blood cell production in the bone marrow, contributing to anemia.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Diagnostic assessment of Francis would probably not reveal:
choices: Abnormal blast cells in the bone marrow
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies leukocytosis as a characteristic finding of CLL, so this is the keyed response for the question as supplied. Note: the wording of this item is internally inconsistent because leukocytosis is expected in CLL.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Robert, a 57-year-old client with acute arterial occlusion of the left leg undergoes an emergency embolectomy. Six hours later, the nurse isn’t able to obtain pulses in his left foot using Doppler ultrasound. The nurse immediately notifies the physician, and asks her to prepare the client for surgery. As the nurse enters the client’s room to prepare him, he states that he won’t have any more surgery. Which of the following is the best initial response by the nurse?
choices: Explain the risks of not having the surgery
Recording the client’s refusal in the nurses’ notes
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The nurse should first explain the risks of refusing the surgery. If the client understands the risks and continues to refuse, the physician and supervisor should be notified and the refusal documented.

pnle-set1-part3.question: During the endorsement, which of the following clients should the on-duty nurse assess first?
choices: The 58-year-old client who was admitted 2 days ago with heart failure, blood pressure of 126/76 mm Hg, and a respiratory rate of 22 breaths/minute.
The 89-year-old client with end-stage right-sided heart failure, blood pressure of 78/50 mm Hg, and a “do not resuscitate” order
The 62-year-old client who was admitted 1 day ago with thrombophlebitis and is receiving I.V. heparin
The 75-year-old client who was admitted 1 hour ago with new-onset atrial fibrillation and is receiving I.V. diltiazem (Cardizem)
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies the client with new-onset atrial fibrillation receiving IV diltiazem as the highest priority because of the potential for instability and the need for close monitoring.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Honey, a 23-year old client complains of substernal chest pain and states that her heart feels like “it’s racing out of the chest”. She reports no history of cardiac disorders. The nurse attaches her to a cardiac monitor and notes sinus tachycardia with a rate of 136beats/minutes. Breath sounds are clear and the respiratory rate is 26 breaths/minutes. Which of the following drugs should the nurse question the client about using?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Cocaine can cause coronary artery spasm, increased myocardial oxygen consumption, tachycardia, ischemia, ventricular dysrhythmias, and myocardial infarction.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 51-year-old female client tells the nurse in-charge that she has found a painless lump in her right breast during her monthly self-examination. Which assessment finding would strongly suggest that this client’s lump is cancerous?
choices: Eversion of the right nipple and mobile mass
Mobile mass that is soft and easily delineated
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A breast cancer mass is more likely to be fixed, hard, and irregular. A soft, mobile, well-defined mass is more consistent with a benign cyst.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 35-year-old client with vaginal cancer asks the nurse, “What is the usual treatment for this type of cancer?” Which treatment should the nurse name?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies external or intravaginal radiation therapy as the usual treatment for vaginal cancer.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Cristina undergoes a biopsy of a suspicious lesion. The biopsy report classifies the lesion according to the TNM staging system as follows: TIS, N0, M0. What does this classification mean?
choices: No evidence of primary tumor, no abnormal regional lymph nodes, and no evidence of distant metastasis
Carcinoma in situ, no abnormal regional lymph nodes, and no evidence of distant metastasis
Can’t assess tumor or regional lymph nodes and no evidence of metastasis
Carcinoma in situ, no demonstrable metastasis of the regional lymph nodes, and ascending degrees of distant metastasis
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Tis indicates carcinoma in situ, N0 indicates no regional lymph-node involvement, and M0 indicates no distant metastasis.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Lydia undergoes a laryngectomy to treat laryngeal cancer. When teaching the client how to care for the neck stoma, the nurse should include which instruction?
choices: “Have a family member perform stoma care initially until you get used to the procedure.”
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source instructs the client to keep the stoma moist to reduce irritation. A stoma bib can also help filter and warm inhaled air.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 37-year-old client with uterine cancer asks the nurse, “Which is the most common type of cancer in women?” The nurse replies that it’s breast cancer. Which type of cancer causes the most deaths in women?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies lung cancer as the leading cause of cancer death in women, with breast cancer ranking second.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Antonio with lung cancer develops Horner’s syndrome when the tumor invades the ribs and affects the sympathetic nerve ganglia. When assessing for signs and symptoms of this syndrome, the nurse should note:
choices: miosis, partial eyelid ptosis, and anhidrosis on the affected side of the face.
chest pain, dyspnea, cough, weight loss, and fever.
arm and shoulder pain and atrophy of arm and hand muscles, both on the affected side.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Horner’s syndrome is characterized by miosis, partial ptosis, and anhidrosis on the affected side of the face.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Vic asks the nurse what PSA is. The nurse should reply that it stands for:
choices: prostate-specific antigen, which is used to screen for prostate cancer.
protein serum antigen, which is used to determine protein levels.
pneumococcal strep antigen, which is a bacteria that causes pneumonia.
Papanicolaou-specific antigen, which is used to screen for cervical cancer.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: PSA stands for prostate-specific antigen. The source describes it as a test used to screen for prostate cancer.

pnle-set1-part3.question: What is the most important postoperative instruction that nurse Kate must give a client who has just returned from the operating room after receiving a subarachnoid block?
choices: “Avoid drinking liquids until the gag reflex returns.”
“Notify a nurse if you experience blood in your urine.”
“Remain supine for the time specified by the physician.”
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source instructs the client to remain supine for the time specified after a subarachnoid block to reduce the risk of spinal headache.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client suspected of having colorectal cancer will require which diagnostic study to confirm the diagnosis?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies sigmoidoscopy as a diagnostic study that helps visualize the lower GI tract and detect colorectal cancer. Stool testing and CEA are not confirming tests, while CT is used for staging.

pnle-set1-part3.question: During a breast examination, which finding most strongly suggests that Luz has breast cancer?
choices: A fixed nodular mass with dimpling of the overlying skin
Multiple firm, round, freely movable masses that change with the menstrual cycle
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A fixed nodular mass with skin dimpling strongly suggests breast malignancy. The other findings are more commonly benign or nonspecific in the source.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A female client with cancer is being evaluated for possible metastasis. Which of the following is one of the most common metastasis sites for cancer cells?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The liver is one of the common sites of cancer metastasis. Other major sites include lymph nodes, lungs, bones, and brain.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Mandy is preparing a client for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to confirm or rule out a spinal cord lesion. During the MRI scan, which of the following would pose a threat to the client?
choices: The client wears a watch and wedding band.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: MRI uses a strong magnetic field, so metal objects such as watches and wedding rings must be removed because they can become dangerous projectiles or cause injury.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Cecile is teaching a female client about preventing osteoporosis. Which of the following teaching points is correct?
choices: Obtaining an X-ray of the bones every 3 years is recommended to detect bone loss.
To avoid fractures, the client should avoid strenuous exercise.
The recommended daily allowance of calcium may be found in a wide variety of foods.
Obtaining the recommended daily allowance of calcium requires taking a calcium supplement.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The recommended calcium intake can often be obtained through a variety of foods. Supplements are not always necessary, and ordinary X-rays are not sensitive for early bone loss.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Before Jacob undergoes arthroscopy, the nurse reviews the assessment findings for contraindications for this procedure. Which finding is a contraindication?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies joint flexion of less than 50% as a contraindication because it can create technical difficulty in inserting and viewing with the arthroscope.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mr. Rodriguez is admitted with severe pain in the knees. Which form of arthritis is characterized by urate deposits and joint pain, usually in the feet and legs, and occurs primarily in men over age 30?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Gouty arthritis is characterized by urate crystal deposits and painful inflammation, commonly affecting the feet and legs.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A heparin infusion at 1,500 unit/hour is ordered for a 64-year-old client with stroke in evolution. The infusion contains 25,000 units of heparin in 500 ml of saline solution. How many milliliters per hour should be given?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The solution contains 25,000 units in 500 mL, or 50 units/mL. At 1,500 units/hour, the required rate is 1,500 ÷ 50 = 30 mL/hour.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 76-year-old male client had a thromboembolic right stroke; his left arm is swollen. Which of the following conditions may cause swelling after a stroke?
choices: Loss of muscle contraction decreasing venous return
Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) due to immobility of the ipsilateral side
Hypoalbuminemia due to protein escaping from an inflamed glomerulus
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: After hemiplegia or hemiparesis, loss of muscle contraction can decrease venous return and contribute to swelling of the affected extremity.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Heberden’s nodes are a common sign of osteoarthritis. Which of the following statement is correct about this deformity?
choices: It appears on the distal interphalangeal joint
It appears on the proximal interphalangeal joint
It appears on the dorsolateral aspect of the interphalangeal joint.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Heberden’s nodes occur at the distal interphalangeal joints. Bouchard’s nodes involve the proximal interphalangeal joints.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Which of the following statements explains the main difference between rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis?
choices: Osteoarthritis is gender-specific, rheumatoid arthritis isn’t
Osteoarthritis is a localized disease rheumatoid arthritis is systemic
Osteoarthritis is a systemic disease, rheumatoid arthritis is localized
Osteoarthritis has dislocations and subluxations, rheumatoid arthritis doesn’t
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Osteoarthritis is primarily a localized degenerative joint disease, whereas rheumatoid arthritis is a systemic autoimmune disease.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mrs. Cruz uses a cane for assistance in walking. Which of the following statements is true about a cane or other assistive devices?
choices: A walker is a better choice than a cane.
The cane should be used on the affected side
The cane should be used on the unaffected side
A client with osteoarthritis should be encouraged to ambulate without the cane
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A cane is generally held on the unaffected side so it can support the weaker or affected side during ambulation.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client with type 1 diabetes is scheduled to receive 30 U of 70/30 insulin. There is no 70/30 insulin available. As a substitution, the nurse may give the client:
choices: 9 U regular insulin and 21 U neutral protamine Hagedorn (NPH).
21 U regular insulin and 9 U NPH.
10 U regular insulin and 20 U NPH.
20 U regular insulin and 10 U NPH.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: 70/30 insulin contains 70% NPH and 30% regular insulin. For 30 units, that is 21 units NPH and 9 units regular insulin.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Len should expect to administer which medication to a client with gout?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Colchicine is used to reduce inflammation associated with acute gout. The other listed medications are not standard treatment for the acute gout attack described.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mr. Domingo with a history of hypertension is diagnosed with primary hyperaldosteronism. This diagnosis indicates that the client’s hypertension is caused by excessive hormone secretion from which of the following glands?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Aldosterone is produced by the adrenal cortex. Excess aldosterone promotes sodium retention and contributes to hypertension.

pnle-set1-part3.question: For a diabetic male client with a foot ulcer, the doctor orders bed rest, a wet-to-dry dressing change every shift, and blood glucose monitoring before meals and bedtime. Why are wet-to-dry dressings used for this client?
choices: They contain exudate and provide a moist wound environment.
They protect the wound from mechanical trauma and promote healing.
They debride the wound and promote healing by secondary intention.
They prevent the entrance of microorganisms and minimize wound discomfort.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Wet-to-dry dressings mechanically debride exudate and necrotic tissue when removed, supporting healing by secondary intention.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Zeny is caring for a client in acute addisonian crisis. Which laboratory data would the nurse expect to find?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Adrenal insufficiency causes decreased aldosterone, leading to sodium loss and potassium retention, so hyperkalemia is expected.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A client is admitted for treatment of the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH). Which nursing intervention is appropriate?
choices: Infusing I.V. fluids rapidly as ordered
Administering glucose-containing I.V. fluids as ordered
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: SIADH causes excessive water retention, so fluid restriction is an appropriate intervention to reduce worsening dilutional hyponatremia and fluid overload.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A female client tells nurse Nikki that she has been working hard for the last 3 months to control her type 2 diabetes mellitus with diet and exercise. To determine the effectiveness of the client’s efforts, the nurse should check:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) reflects average blood glucose control over approximately the preceding 3 months.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Trinity administered neutral protamine Hagedorn (NPH) insulin to a diabetic client at 7 a.m. At what time would the nurse expect the client to be most at risk for a hypoglycemic reaction?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: NPH is intermediate-acting and peaks approximately 8 to 12 hours after administration. A 7 a.m. dose therefore places the client at greatest risk during the afternoon.

pnle-set1-part3.question: The adrenal cortex is responsible for producing which substances?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The adrenal cortex produces glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, and androgens. Catecholamines such as epinephrine and norepinephrine are produced by the adrenal medulla.

pnle-set1-part3.question: On the third day after a partial thyroidectomy, Proserfina exhibits muscle twitching and hyperirritability of the nervous system. When questioned, the client reports numbness and tingling of the mouth and fingertips. Suspecting a life-threatening electrolyte disturbance, the nurse notifies the surgeon immediately. Which electrolyte disturbance most commonly follows thyroid surgery?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Accidental injury or removal of the parathyroid glands during thyroid surgery can cause hypocalcemia, producing tingling, twitching, and neuromuscular irritability.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Which laboratory test value is elevated in clients who smoke and can’t be used as a general indicator of cancer?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) can be elevated in smokers, so it is not specific enough to serve as a general cancer indicator. It can still be useful for monitoring certain cancers.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Francis with anemia has been admitted to the medical-surgical unit. Which assessment findings are characteristic of iron-deficiency anemia?
choices: Nights sweats, weight loss, and diarrhea
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Iron-deficiency anemia commonly causes pallor, tachycardia, dyspnea, fatigue, weakness, and headache because of reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.

pnle-set1-part3.question: In teaching a female client who is HIV-positive about pregnancy, the nurse would know more teaching is necessary when the client says:
choices: The baby can get the virus from my placenta.”
“I’m planning on starting on birth control pills.”
“Not everyone who has the virus gives birth to a baby who has the virus.”
“I’ll need to have a C-section if I become pregnant and have a baby.”
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies the statement about needing a C-section simply because of HIV infection as requiring more teaching.

pnle-set1-part3.question: When preparing Judy with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) for discharge to the home, the nurse should be sure to include which instruction?
choices: “Sterilize all plates and utensils in boiling water.”
“Avoid sharing such articles as toothbrushes and razors.”
“Avoid eating foods from serving dishes shared by other family members.”
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: HIV is concentrated in blood, so personal items that may become blood-contaminated, such as toothbrushes and razors, should not be shared.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Marie is caring for a 32-year-old client admitted with pernicious anemia. Which set of findings should the nurse expect when assessing the client?
choices: Pallor, bradycardia, and reduced pulse pressure
Pallor, tachycardia, and a sore tongue
Sore tongue, dyspnea, and weight gain
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Pernicious anemia can cause pallor, tachycardia, weakness, fatigue, and a smooth, sore tongue. Neurologic symptoms such as paresthesias may also occur.

pnle-set1-part3.question: After receiving a dose of penicillin, a client develops dyspnea and hypotension. Nurse Celestina suspects the client is experiencing anaphylactic shock. What should the nurse do first?
choices: Page an anesthesiologist immediately and prepare to intubate the client.
Administer epinephrine, as prescribed, and prepare to intubate the client if necessary.
Administer the antidote for penicillin, as prescribed, and continue to monitor the client’s vital signs.
Insert an indwelling urinary catheter and begin to infuse I.V. fluids as ordered.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Epinephrine is the first-line medication for anaphylaxis. Airway support and additional fluid or medication therapy may follow as clinically indicated.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Mr. Marquez with rheumatoid arthritis is about to begin aspirin therapy to reduce inflammation. When teaching the client about aspirin, the nurse discusses adverse reactions to prolonged aspirin therapy. These include:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Prolonged salicylate use can cause tinnitus and hearing changes. The source identifies bilateral hearing loss as an adverse effect that can resolve after discontinuation.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A 23-year-old client is diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). After recovering from the initial shock of the diagnosis, the client expresses a desire to learn as much as possible about HIV and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). When teaching the client about the immune system, the nurse states that adaptive immunity is provided by which type of white blood cell?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Adaptive immunity is mediated by B and T lymphocytes, which recognize antigens and form immunologic memory.

pnle-set1-part3.question: In an individual with Sjögren’s syndrome, nursing care should focus on:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Sjögren’s syndrome causes loss of lubrication and dryness of mucosal and other tissues, so moisture replacement is a major focus of care.

pnle-set1-part3.question: During chemotherapy for lymphocytic leukemia, Mathew develops abdominal pain, fever, and “horse barn” smelling diarrhea. It would be most important for the nurse to advise the physician to order:
choices: flat plate X-ray of the abdomen.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Chemotherapy and immunosuppression increase the risk of C. difficile infection. A stool test is needed to evaluate this likely cause of characteristic diarrhea.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client seeks medical evaluation for fatigue, night sweats, and a 20-lb weight loss in 6 weeks. To confirm that the client has been infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), the nurse expects the physician to order:
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The supplied source uses the historical testing sequence of ELISA followed by Western blot confirmation for HIV antibodies.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A complete blood count is commonly performed before a Joe goes into surgery. What does this test seek to identify?
choices: Potential hepatic dysfunction indicated by decreased blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and creatinine levels
Low levels of urine constituents normally excreted in the urine
Abnormally low hematocrit (HCT) and hemoglobin (Hb) levels
Electrolyte imbalance that could affect the blood’s ability to coagulate properly
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A CBC provides hemoglobin and hematocrit values and can identify anemia or blood loss risk before surgery.

pnle-set1-part3.question: While monitoring a client for the development of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), the nurse should take note of what assessment parameters?
choices: Platelet count, prothrombin time, and partial thromboplastin time
Platelet count, blood glucose levels, and white blood cell (WBC) count
Thrombin time, calcium levels, and potassium levels
Fibrinogen level, WBC, and platelet count
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: DIC is evaluated with coagulation studies and platelet counts, including PT and PTT. Fibrinogen and thrombin time may also be assessed.

pnle-set1-part3.question: When taking a dietary history from a newly admitted female client, Nurse Len should remember that which of the following foods is a common allergen?
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The supplied source identifies strawberries and other berries as common food allergens among the listed choices.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse John is caring for clients in the outpatient clinic. Which of the following phone calls should the nurse return first?
choices: A client with hepatitis A who states, “My arms and legs are itching.”
A client with cast on the right leg who states, “I have a funny feeling in my right leg.”
A client with osteomyelitis of the spine who states, “I am so nauseous that I can’t eat.”
A client with rheumatoid arthritis who states, “I am having trouble sleeping.”
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A new unusual sensation in a limb with a cast can indicate neurovascular compromise and requires prompt assessment.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Sarah is caring for clients on the surgical floor and has just received report from the previous shift. Which of the following clients should the nurse see first?
choices: A 35-year-old admitted three hours ago with a gunshot wound; 1.5 cm area of dark drainage noted on the dressing.
A 43-year-old who had a mastectomy two days ago; 23 ml of serosanguinous fluid noted in the Jackson-Pratt drain.
A 59-year-old with a collapsed lung due to an accident; no drainage noted in the previous eight hours.
A 62-year-old who had an abdominal-perineal resection three days ago; client complaints of chills.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source prioritizes the client with chills three days after abdominal-perineal resection because this may indicate postoperative infection or peritonitis and requires assessment.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Eve is caring for a client who had a thyroidectomy 12 hours ago for treatment of Grave’s disease. The nurse would be most concerned if which of the following was observed?
choices: Blood pressure 138/82, respirations 16, oral temperature 99 degrees Fahrenheit.
The client supports his head and neck when turning his head to the right.
The client spontaneously flexes his wrist when the blood pressure is obtained.
The client is drowsy and complains of sore throat.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Spontaneous wrist flexion or carpal spasm during blood-pressure measurement suggests hypocalcemia, which can occur after thyroidectomy if the parathyroids are affected.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Julius is admitted with complaints of severe pain in the lower right quadrant of the abdomen. To assist with pain relief, the nurse should take which of the following actions?
choices: Encourage the client to change positions frequently in bed.
Administer Demerol 50 mg IM q 4 hours and PRN.
Apply warmth to the abdomen with a heating pad.
Use comfort measures and pillows to position the client.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The supplied source identifies nonpharmacologic comfort measures and supportive positioning with pillows as the appropriate pain-relief action.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Tina prepares a client for peritoneal dialysis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
choices: Assess for a bruit and a thrill.
Position the client on the left side.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The dialysate should be warmed to body temperature to reduce discomfort during peritoneal dialysis. The source specifically identifies warming the solution as the first action.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Jannah teaches an elderly client with right-sided weakness how to use cane. Which of the following behaviors, if demonstrated by the client to the nurse, indicates that the teaching was effective?
choices: The client holds the cane with his right hand, moves the can forward followed by the right leg, and then moves the left leg.
The client holds the cane with his right hand, moves the cane forward followed by his left leg, and then moves the right leg.
The client holds the cane with his left hand, moves the cane forward followed by the right leg, and then moves the left leg.
The client holds the cane with his left hand, moves the cane forward followed by his left leg, and then moves the right leg.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The cane should be held on the unaffected left side. The cane moves forward first, followed by the weaker right leg and then the left leg.

pnle-set1-part3.question: An elderly client is admitted to the nursing home setting. The client is occasionally confused and her gait is often unsteady. Which of the following actions, if taken by the nurse, is most appropriate?
choices: Ask the woman’s family to provide personal items such as photos or mementos.
Select a room with a bed by the door so the woman can look down the hall.
Suggest the woman eat her meals in the room with her roommate.
Encourage the woman to ambulate in the halls twice a day.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Photos and familiar mementos provide visual stimulation and help reduce sensory deprivation in an older adult.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Evangeline teaches an elderly client how to use a standard aluminum walker. Which of the following behaviors, if demonstrated by the client, indicates that the nurse’s teaching was effective?
choices: The client slowly pushes the walker forward 12 inches, then takes small steps forward while leaning on the walker.
The client lifts the walker, moves it forward 10 inches, and then takes several small steps forward.
The client supports his weight on the walker while advancing it forward, then takes small steps while balancing on the walker.
The client slides the walker 18 inches forward, then takes small steps while holding onto the walker for balance.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: A standard walker is lifted, placed forward on all legs, and then followed by small steps while maintaining balance.

pnle-set1-part3.question: Nurse Deric is supervising a group of elderly clients in a residential home setting. The nurse knows that the elderly are at greater risk of developing sensory deprivation for what reason?
choices: Increased sensitivity to the side effects of medications.
Decreased visual, auditory, and gustatory abilities.
Isolation from their families and familiar surroundings.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: The source identifies isolation from family and familiar surroundings as the reason for increased risk of sensory deprivation in this item.

pnle-set1-part3.question: A male client with emphysema becomes restless and confused. What step should nurse Jasmine take next?
choices: Encourage the client to perform pursed lip breathing.
Increase the client’s oxygen flow rate.
pnle-set1-part3.explanation: Pursed-lip breathing helps prevent airway collapse and helps control the rate and depth of breathing in emphysema.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Randy has undergone kidney transplant, what assessment would prompt Nurse Katrina to suspect organ rejection?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Hypertension, along with fever, and tenderness over the grafted kidney, reflects acute rejection.

pnle-set1-part4.question: The immediate objective of nursing care for an overweight, mildly hypertensive male client with ureteral colic and hematuria is to decrease:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Sharp, severe pain (renal colic) radiating toward the genitalia and thigh is caused by uretheral distention and smooth muscle spasm; relief form pain is the priority.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Matilda, with hyperthyroidism is to receive Lugol’s iodine solution before a subtotal thyroidectomy is performed. The nurse is aware that this medication is given to:
choices: Decrease the total basal metabolic rate.
Maintain the function of the parathyroid glands.
Block the formation of thyroxine by the thyroid gland.
Decrease the size and vascularity of the thyroid gland.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Lugol’s solution provides iodine, which aids in decreasing the vascularity of the thyroid gland, which limits the risk of hemorrhage when surgery is performed.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Ricardo, was diagnosed with type I diabetes. The nurse is aware that acute hypoglycemia also can develop in the client who is diagnosed with:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The client with liver disease has a decreased ability to metabolize carbohydrates because of a decreased ability to form glycogen (glycogenesis) and to form glucose from glycogen.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Tracy is receiving combination chemotherapy for treatment of metastatic carcinoma. Nurse Ruby should monitor the client for the systemic side effect of:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Leukopenia, a reduction in WBCs, is a systemic effect of chemotherapy as a result of myelosuppression.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Norma, with recent colostomy expresses concern about the inability to control the passage of gas. Nurse Oliver should suggest that the client plan to:
choices: Decrease fluid intake at meal times.
Avoid foods that in the past caused flatus.
Adhere to a bland diet prior to social events.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Foods that bothered a person preoperatively will continue to do so after a colostomy.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Ron begins to teach a male client how to perform colostomy irrigations. The nurse would evaluate that the instructions were understood when the client states, “I should:
choices: Lie on my left side while instilling the irrigating solution.”
Keep the irrigating container less than 18 inches above the stoma.”
Instill a minimum of 1200 ml of irrigating solution to stimulate evacuation of the bowel.”
Insert the irrigating catheter deeper into the stoma if cramping occurs during the procedure.”
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: This height permits the solution to flow slowly with little force so that excessive peristalsis is not immediately precipitated.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Patrick is in the oliguric phase of acute tubular necrosis and is experiencing fluid and electrolyte imbalances. The client is somewhat confused and complains of nausea and muscle weakness. As part of the prescribed therapy to correct this electrolyte imbalance, the nurse would expect to:
choices: Increase oral intake of cheese and milk.
Administer large amounts of normal saline via I.V.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Kayexalate, a potassium exchange resin, permits sodium to be exchanged for potassium in the intestine, reducing the serum potassium level.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Mario has burn injury. After Forty48 hours, the physician orders for Mario 2 liters of IV fluid to be administered q12 h. The drop factor of the tubing is 10 gtt/ml. The nurse should set the flow to provide:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: This is the correct flow rate; multiply the amount to be infused (2000 ml) by the drop factor (10) and divide the result by the amount of time in minutes (12 hours x 60 minutes).

pnle-set1-part4.question: Terence suffered form burn injury. Using the rule of nines, which has the largest percent of burns?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The percentage designated for each burned part of the body using the rule of nines: Head and neck 9%; Right upper extremity 9%; Left upper extremity 9%; Anterior trunk 18%; Posterior trunk 18%; Right lower extremity 18%; Left lower extremity 18%; Perineum 1%.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Herbert, a 45 year old construction engineer is brought to the hospital unconscious after falling from a 2-story building. When assessing the client, the nurse would be most concerned if the assessment revealed:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The nurse needs to perform a thorough assessment that could indicate alterations in cerebral function, increased intracranial pressures, fractures and bleeding. Bleeding from the ears occurs only with basal skull fractures that can easily contribute to increased intracranial pressure and brain herniation.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Sherry is teaching male client regarding his permanent artificial pacemaker. Which information given by the nurse shows her knowledge deficit about the artificial cardiac pacemaker?
choices: take the pulse rate once a day, in the morning upon awakening
May be allowed to use electrical appliances
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The client should be advised by the nurse to avoid contact sports. This will prevent trauma to the area of the pacemaker generator.

pnle-set1-part4.question: The nurse is ware that the most relevant knowledge about oxygen administration to a male client with COPD is
choices: Oxygen at 1-2L/min is given to maintain the hypoxic stimulus for breathing.
Hypoxia stimulates the central chemoreceptors in the medulla that makes the client breath.
Oxygen is administered best using a non-rebreathing mask
Blood gases are monitored using a pulse oximeter.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: COPD causes a chronic CO2 retention that renders the medulla insensitive to the CO2 stimulation for breathing. The hypoxic state of the client then becomes the stimulus for breathing. Giving the client oxygen in low concentrations will maintain the client’s hypoxic drive.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Tonny has undergoes a left thoracotomy and a partial pneumonectomy. Chest tubes are inserted, and one-bottle water-seal drainage is instituted in the operating room. In the postanesthesia care unit Tonny is placed in Fowler’s position on either his right side or on his back. The nurse is aware that this position:
choices: Facilitate ventilation of the left lung.
Equalize pressure in the pleural space.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Since only a partial pneumonectomy is done, there is a need to promote expansion of this remaining Left lung by positioning the client on the opposite unoperated side.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Kristine is scheduled for a bronchoscopy. When teaching Kristine what to expect afterward, the nurse’s highest priority of information would be:
choices: Food and fluids will be withheld for at least 2 hours.
Warm saline gargles will be done q 2h.
Coughing and deep-breathing exercises will be done q2h.
Only ice chips and cold liquids will be allowed initially.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Prior to bronchoscopy, the doctors sprays the back of the throat with anesthetic to minimize the gag reflex and thus facilitate the insertion of the bronchoscope. Giving the client food and drink after the procedure without checking on the return of the gag reflex can cause the client to aspirate. The gag reflex usually returns after two hours.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Tristan is caring for a male client in acute renal failure. The nurse should expect hypertonic glucose, insulin infusions, and sodium bicarbonate to be used to treat:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Hyperkalemia is a common complication of acute renal failure. It’s life-threatening if immediate action isn’t taken to reverse it. The administration of glucose and regular insulin, with sodium bicarbonate if necessary, can temporarily prevent cardiac arrest by moving potassium into the cells and temporarily reducing serum potassium levels. Hypernatremia, hypokalemia, and hypercalcemia don’t usually occur with acute renal failure and aren’t treated with glucose, insulin, or sodium bicarbonate.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Ms. X has just been diagnosed with condylomata acuminata (genital warts). What information is appropriate to tell this client?
choices: This condition puts her at a higher risk for cervical cancer; therefore, she should have a Papanicolaou (Pap) smear annually.
The most common treatment is metronidazole (Flagyl), which should eradicate the problem within 7 to 10 days.
The potential for transmission to her sexual partner will be eliminated if condoms are used every time they have sexual intercourse.
The human papillomavirus (HPV), which causes condylomata acuminata, can’t be transmitted during oral sex.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Women with condylomata acuminata are at risk for cancer of the cervix and vulva. Yearly Pap smears are very important for early detection. Because condylomata acuminata is a virus, there is no permanent cure. Because condylomata acuminata can occur on the vulva, a condom won’t protect sexual partners. HPV can be transmitted to other parts of the body, such as the mouth, oropharynx, and larynx.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Maritess was recently diagnosed with a genitourinary problem and is being examined in the emergency department. When palpating the her kidneys, the nurse should keep which anatomical fact in mind?
choices: The left kidney usually is slightly higher than the right one.
The kidneys are situated just above the adrenal glands.
The average kidney is approximately 5 cm (2″) long and 2 to 3 cm (¾” to 1-1/8″) wide.
The kidneys lie between the 10th and 12th thoracic vertebrae.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The left kidney usually is slightly higher than the right one. An adrenal gland lies atop each kidney. The average kidney measures approximately 11 cm (4-3/8″) long, 5 to 5.8 cm (2″ to 2¼”) wide, and 2.5 cm (1″) thick. The kidneys are located retroperitoneally, in the posterior aspect of the abdomen, on either side of the vertebral column. They lie between the 12th thoracic and 3rd lumbar vertebrae.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Jestoni with chronic renal failure (CRF) is admitted to the urology unit. The nurse is aware that the diagnostic test are consistent with CRF if the result is:
choices: Increased pH with decreased hydrogen ions.
Increased serum levels of potassium, magnesium, and calcium.
Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 100 mg/dl and serum creatinine 6.5 mg/ dl.
Uric acid analysis 3.5 mg/dl and phenolsulfonphthalein (PSP) excretion 75%.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The normal BUN level ranges 8 to 23 mg/dl; the normal serum creatinine level ranges from 0.7 to 1.5 mg/dl. The test results in option C are abnormally elevated, reflecting CRF and the kidneys’ decreased ability to remove nonprotein nitrogen waste from the blood. CRF causes decreased pH and increased hydrogen ions — not vice versa. CRF also increases serum levels of potassium, magnesium, and phosphorous, and decreases serum levels of calcium. A uric acid analysis of 3.5 mg/dl falls within the normal range of 2.7 to 7.7 mg/dl; PSP excretion of 75% also falls with the normal range of 60% to 75%.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Katrina has an abnormal result on a Papanicolaou test. After admitting that she read her chart while the nurse was out of the room, Katrina asks what dysplasia means. Which definition should the nurse provide?
choices: Presence of completely undifferentiated tumor cells that don’t resemble cells of the tissues of their origin.
Increase in the number of normal cells in a normal arrangement in a tissue or an organ.
Replacement of one type of fully differentiated cell by another in tissues where the second type normally isn’t found.
Alteration in the size, shape, and organization of differentiated cells.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Dysplasia refers to an alteration in the size, shape, and organization of differentiated cells. The presence of completely undifferentiated tumor cells that don’t resemble cells of the tissues of their origin is called anaplasia. An increase in the number of normal cells in a normal arrangement in a tissue or an organ is called hyperplasia. Replacement of one type of fully differentiated cell by another in tissues where the second type normally isn’t found is called metaplasia.

pnle-set1-part4.question: During a routine checkup, Nurse Mariane assesses a male client with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) for signs and symptoms of cancer. What is the most common AIDS-related cancer?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Kaposi’s sarcoma is the most common cancer associated with AIDS. Squamous cell carcinoma, multiple myeloma, and leukemia may occur in anyone and aren’t associated specifically with AIDS.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Ricardo is scheduled for a prostatectomy, and the anesthesiologist plans to use a spinal (subarachnoid) block during surgery. In the operating room, the nurse positions the client according to the anesthesiologist’s instructions. Why does the client require special positioning for this type of anesthesia?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The client receiving a subarachnoid block requires special positioning to prevent CSF leakage and headache and to ensure proper anesthetic distribution. Proper positioning doesn’t help prevent confusion, seizures, or cardiac arrhythmias.

pnle-set1-part4.question: A male client had a nephrectomy 2 days ago and is now complaining of abdominal pressure and nausea. The first nursing action should be to:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: If abdominal distention is accompanied by nausea, the nurse must first auscultate bowel sounds. If bowel sounds are absent, the nurse should suspect gastric or small intestine dilation and these findings must be reported to the physician. Palpation should be avoided postoperatively with abdominal distention. If peristalsis is absent, changing positions and inserting a rectal tube won’t relieve the client’s discomfort.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Wilfredo with a recent history of rectal bleeding is being prepared for a colonoscopy. How should the nurse Patricia position the client for this test initially?
choices: Lying on the right side with legs straight
Lying on the left side with knees bent
Bent over with hands touching the floor
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: For a colonoscopy, the nurse initially should position the client on the left side with knees bent. Placing the client on the right side with legs straight, prone with the torso elevated, or bent over with hands touching the floor wouldn’t allow proper visualization of the large intestine.

pnle-set1-part4.question: A male client with inflammatory bowel disease undergoes an ileostomy. On the first day after surgery, Nurse Oliver notes that the client’s stoma appears dusky. How should the nurse interpret this finding?
choices: Blood supply to the stoma has been interrupted.
This is a normal finding 1 day after surgery.
The ostomy bag should be adjusted.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: An ileostomy stoma forms as the ileum is brought through the abdominal wall to the surface skin, creating an artificial opening for waste elimination. The stoma should appear cherry red, indicating adequate arterial perfusion. A dusky stoma suggests decreased perfusion, which may result from interruption of the stoma’s blood supply and may lead to tissue damage or necrosis. A dusky stoma isn’t a normal finding. Adjusting the ostomy bag wouldn’t affect stoma color, which depends on blood supply to the area. An intestinal obstruction also wouldn’t change stoma color.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Anthony suffers burns on the legs, which nursing intervention helps prevent contractures?
choices: Elevating the foot of the bed
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Applying knee splints prevents leg contractures by holding the joints in a position of function. Elevating the foot of the bed can’t prevent contractures because this action doesn’t hold the joints in a position of function. Hyperextending a body part for an extended time is inappropriate because it can cause contractures. Performing shoulder range-of-motion exercises can prevent contractures in the shoulders, but not in the legs.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Ron is assessing a client admitted with second- and third-degree burns on the face, arms, and chest. Which finding indicates a potential problem?
choices: Partial pressure of arterial oxygen (PaO2) value of 80 mm Hg.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: A urine output of less than 40 ml/hour in a client with burns indicates a fluid volume deficit. This client’s PaO2 value falls within the normal range (80 to 100 mm Hg). White pulmonary secretions also are normal. The client’s rectal temperature isn’t significantly elevated and probably results from the fluid volume deficit.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Mr. Mendoza who has suffered a cerebrovascular accident (CVA) is too weak to move on his own. To help the client avoid pressure ulcers, Nurse Celia should:
choices: Encourage the client to use a footboard.
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: The most important intervention to prevent pressure ulcers is frequent position changes, which relieve pressure on the skin and underlying tissues. If pressure isn’t relieved, capillaries become occluded, reducing circulation and oxygenation of the tissues and resulting in cell death and ulcer formation. During passive ROM exercises, the nurse moves each joint through its range of movement, which improves joint mobility and circulation to the affected area but doesn’t prevent pressure ulcers. Adequate hydration is necessary to maintain healthy skin and ensure tissue repair. A footboard prevents plantar flexion and footdrop by maintaining the foot in a dorsiflexed position.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Maria plans to administer dexamethasone cream to a female client who has dermatitis over the anterior chest. How should the nurse apply this topical agent?
choices: With a circular motion, to enhance absorption.
With an upward motion, to increase blood supply to the affected area
In long, even, outward, and downward strokes in the direction of hair growth
In long, even, outward, and upward strokes in the direction opposite hair growth
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: When applying a topical agent, the nurse should begin at the midline and use long, even, outward, and downward strokes in the direction of hair growth. This application pattern reduces the risk of follicle irritation and skin inflammation.

pnle-set1-part4.question: Nurse Kate is aware that one of the following classes of medication protect the ischemic myocardium by blocking catecholamines and sympathetic nerve stimulation is:
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Beta-adrenergic blockers work by blocking beta receptors in the myocardium, reducing the response to catecholamines and sympathetic nerve stimulation. They protect the myocardium, helping to reduce the risk of another infraction by decreasing myocardial oxygen demand. Calcium channel blockers reduce the workload of the heart by decreasing the heart rate. Narcotics reduce myocardial oxygen demand, promote vasodilation, and decrease anxiety. Nitrates reduce myocardial oxygen consumption bt decreasing left ventricular end diastolic pressure (preload) and systemic vascular resistance (afterload).

pnle-set1-part4.question: A male client has jugular distention. On what position should the nurse place the head of the bed to obtain the most accurate reading of jugular vein distention?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Jugular venous pressure is measured with a centimeter ruler to obtain the vertical distance between the sternal angle and the point of highest pulsation with the head of the bed inclined between 15 to 30 degrees. Increased pressure can’t be seen when the client is supine or when the head of the bed is raised 10 degrees because the point that marks the pressure level is above the jaw (therefore, not visible). In high Fowler’s position, the veins would be barely discernible above the clavicle.

pnle-set1-part4.question: The nurse is aware that one of the following classes of medications maximizes cardiac performance in clients with heart failure by increasing ventricular contractility?
pnle-set1-part4.explanation: Inotropic agents are administered to increase the force of the heart’s contractions, thereby increasing ventricular contractility and ultimately increasing cardiac output. Beta-adrenergic blockers and calcium channel blockers decrease the heart rate and ultimately decreased the workload of the heart. Diuretics are administered to decrease the overall vascular volume, also decreasing the workload of the heart.

pnle-set1-part4.question: A male client has a reduced serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL) level and an elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) level. Which of the following dietary modifications is not appropriate for this client?
choices: Fiber intake of 25 to 30 g daily
Less than 30% of calories form fat
Cholesterol intake of less than 300 mg daily
Less than 10% of calories from saturated fat
